L202: ## Overview
L203: 
L204: The Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma program combines computer systems theory with hands-on practical experience in software development. This diploma is a widely recognized credential that employers highly regard. You'll emerge with the well-rounded skills essential for a career analyzing, designing, and developing software solutions.
L205: 
L206: cite88†BCIT Computer Systems Technology (CST) Info Session†youtu.be L207: In two years, you’ll learn software engineering and programming from industry professionals, and gain experience working on real projects, from concept to deployment. In your second year, specialty options and industry projects add depth to further hone your skills.
L208: ### About the program
L209:   * Work through this intensive, 2-year full-time program with your cohort, sharing your experience and expertise, and building a professional network that will last long after you graduate.
L210:   * 2 intakes: September & January
L211:   * Monday to Friday, 8:30 am until 5:30 pm – h eavy workload; we recommend students do not work during school terms
L212:   * First year sets the foundation with the core skills you’ll need as a professional software developer – cite89†check out some first-year app projects L213:   * Second-year options allow you to further your skills in specialty areas
L214:   * Work on at least two industry projects with cite90†real clients from industry L215:   * Co-operative Education option for broader applied experience (competitive entry)
L216:   * Engage with an active student community, clubs, and events
L217:   * Excellent job placement rate upon graduation
L218: See the cite67†Program Details to learn more about what you can expect from CST, and how you can prepare for a wide variety of career options in the IT industry.
L219: ### Who should complete the CST Diploma?
L220: 
L221: This program might be for you if:
L222: 
L223:   * You’re interested in software development
L224:   * You enjoy problem-solving, often in teams
L225:   * You’re enthusiastic about using technology, computers, and software systems to make things better
L226:   * You’re ready to apply yourself to prepare for a career in the evolving and rapidly expanding Computing and IT sector
L227: If any of these sound like you, please check the cite63†Entrance Requirements to ensure you can apply and start your new IT career!
L228: ### What Computer Systems Technology grads can do?
L229: 
L230: By earning your BCIT Diploma, you’ll be honing your IT skills and gaining knowledge of various industry-recognized technologies, preparing you for positions in multiple industries and locations.
L231: 
L232: As a CST graduate, you’ll be able to:
L233:   * Participate in all aspects of software development and maintenance
L234:   * Contribute and communicate effectively as a member of software project teams
L235:   * Design and code with widely-used programming languages and scripting tools, which include JavaScript, Python, Java, C, and C++
L236:   * Develop and maintain complex software systems that integrate scalable components, such as Cloud Computing
L237:   * Apply logical, critical, and creative thinking to effectively solve Computing and IT-related problems
L238:   * Synthesize solutions to novel problems using various approaches, including Artificial Intelligence (AI)
L239:   * Work productively and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
L240:   * Independently learn and adopt new tools, current technologies and methods to stay industry-ready.
L241:   * Engage with a well-established alumni community of CST Grads in industry

L177: ## Your path to Red Seal Certification
L178: 
L179: Foundation Apprenticeship Getting started Supports
L180: ### Foundation
L181: 
L182: NIC’s trades cite9†foundation programs equip you with the basic knowledge and skills needed to enter a trade without requiring an employer sponsor.
L183: 
L184: Upon completion of a foundation program, you’ll receive Level 1 technical training and some work-based training hours when you register as an apprentice.
L185: 
L186: Completing a foundation program can make it easier to find employment and sponsorship to continue as an apprentice, since you’re entering the trade with some experience.
L187: ### Apprenticeship
L188: 
L189: Most apprenticeships take four or more years to complete, with 80% of the training at the worksite under the supervision of a certified tradesperson and 20% in-class technical training.
L190: 
L191: You can choose to seek employer sponsorship for an apprenticeship right away or you can complete a foundation program for Level 1 training first.
L192: ### Getting started
L193: 
L194: cite59†Find your trade†skilledtradesbc.ca and become familiar with how many levels of training you need, the number of work-based hours required and information about your exams.
L195: 
L196: ### Supports
L197: 
L198: During your technical training, you are eligible to apply for financial supports with WorkBC Employment Services and Service Canada. Visit SkilledTradesBC for more info.
L199: 
L200: cite60†Learn more†skilledtradesbc.ca L201: 
L202: ## Frequently asked questions
L203: ## [Button: What are the differences of levels for trades training, like Harmonized or Apprenticeship? ]
L204: 
L205: Typically, NIC offers:
L206: 
L207:   * Pre-apprenticeship (Foundation) programs: Level 1 Foundation training to prepare for entry-level positions.
L208:   * Apprenticeship programs: A combination of on-the-job training and classroom instruction, Level 1-4.
L209:   * Specialized certifications: Training in specific skills or safety standards, such as welding or forklift operation.
L210: ## [Button: How do I become an apprentice? ]
L211: 
L212: Visit cite61†SkilledTradesBC†skilledtradesbc.ca to learn how to become an apprentice.
L213: 
L214: ## [Button: Is trades training suitable for women and underrepresented groups? ]
L215: 
L216: Absolutely! Colleges and industries actively encourage diversity in trades.
L217: ## [Button: Can I work while studying trades? ]
L218: 
L219: International students are allowed to work off campus up to 24 hours per week. You can work unlimited hours off campus during scheduled NIC breaks (e.g. reading week, winter holidays).
L220: 
L221: ## [Button: Who can I contact for more information? ]
L222: 
L223: Contact study@nic.bc.ca for guidance on the program, requirements and application procedures.

L198:

L203: cite126†Practical Nursing†www.youtube.com L204: ## What you will learn
L205: 
L206: Upon successful completion of this program, graduates will be able to:
L207:   * Apply the Entry Level Competencies for Licensed Practical Nurses (2021) to provide safe, competent, culturally safe and ethical care.
L208:   * Practice within relevant legislation, BCCNM Standards of Practice for LPNs Framework: Scope of Practice Standards; Professional Standards; and Practice Standards as set out by the Health Professions Act of British Columbia and the British Columbia College of Nurses & Midwives (BCCNM).
L209:   * Value and engage in continuous learning to maintain and enhance competence.
L210:   * Practice in collaboration with other members of the health care team to meet the collective needs of their clients.
L211:   * Participate in interprofessional problem solving and decision making processes.
L212:   * Advocate for and facilitate change reflecting evidence-informed practice.
L213:   * Make practice decisions that are client specific and consider client acuity, complexity, variability, and available resources.
L214:   * Use critical thinking, clinical judgment and knowledge of assessment to plan, implement, and evaluate the agreed upon plan of care.
L215:   * Develop a collaborative relationship with clients by connecting, sharing and exploring with them in a caring environment.
L216:   * Provide culturally safe, person-centered care across the lifespan that recognizes and respects the uniqueness of each individual and is sensitive to cultural safety, cultural humility and diversity.
L217:   * Provide leadership, direction, assignment, and supervision of unregulated care providers as appropriate.
L218:   * Identify one’s own values, biases, and assumptions on interactions with clients and other members of the health care team.
L219: ## What to expect
L220: ### Program Duration and Maximum Time for Completion
L221: 
L222: The Practical Nursing Diploma is sixteen (16) months in length. Students must complete the diploma within three (3) years from the initial start date to the completion date.
L223: This diploma program is offered on a full time basis and is divided into four levels. Each level must be successfully completed before the next one can be started. A major emphasis of this program is active student participation. Throughout the program the instructors will encourage the students to become increasingly more self directed and responsible for their own learning. Students are expected to come to class well prepared for active participation in classroom, nursing lab and clinical activities.

L173:   * The list of priority occupations related to healthcare and construction has been updated, and the program will be expanding the list of ineligible occupations and employers to focus nominations on priorities, strengthen program integrity, and ensure that British Columbians have opportunities in these roles.
L174: More details about the changes will be included in an updated BC PNP Skills Immigration Program Guide which will be posted on the cite20†Documents page in the near future.
L175: Strong Outcomes
L176: Since 2022, the BC PNP shifted to be more strategic in its selection through prioritization of key occupations to support government priorities. The program has nominated:
L177:   * 3,887 healthcare professionals, including 475 doctors and 1,228 nurses and nurse practitioners
L178:   * 2,957 licensed childcare workers
L179:   * 826 construction and trades workers after targeting select certified trades
L180:   * 26 veterinarians and 116 veterinary technologists, many working outside Metro Vancouver
L181:   * Over 38% of Skills Immigration nominees are working in regional communities, supporting population and economic growth across B.C.
L182: Looking Ahead
L183: B.C. continues to advocate to the federal government for increased provincial nominee allocations in 2026 and future years to support public services, major projects and infrastructure, economic growth, and regional communities across the province.

L29:   * cite5†About the PGWP L30:   * cite6†Who can apply L31:     * cite7†Find your language level L32:     * cite8†Field of study requirements L33:   * cite9†Get the right documents L34:   * cite10†How to apply L35:   * cite11†After you apply L36: # Who can apply
L37: 
L38: To be eligible for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP), you must meet all eligibility requirements.
L39: 
L40: Eligibility requirements include
L41:   * cite12†general eligibility L42:   * cite13†eligibility requirements based on study program L43:     * Study program requirements include both
L44:       * proof of language skills
L45:       * field of study requirements (if applicable)
L46:   * cite14†eligibility requirements based on physical location L47:     * inside Canada graduates
L48:     * outside Canada graduates
L49:   * cite15†field of study requirements (if applicable) L50: ## General eligibility
L51: 
L52: You meet the general eligibility requirement to apply for a PGWP if
L53:   * you completed a program of study at a PGWP-eligible cite16†designated learning institution that was at least 8 months long (or 900 hours for Quebec programs)
L54:   * you maintained full-time status as a student in Canada during each semester of your study program
L55:     * You may study part-time during your final semester.
L56:   * you apply for your PGWP within 180 days of confirmation that you completed your program of study
L57:   * your study permit was valid at some point during the 180 days after you completed your program of study
L58: cite17†Check the special cases to learn if exceptions to the general eligibility requirements apply to your situation .
L59: 
L60: Special cases
L61: 
L62: You may also be eligible to apply for a PGWP if you’re in one of the special case groups.
L63: 
L64: Accelerated programs
L65: 
L66: If you complete your study program in less time than the normal length of the program, you may be eligible for a PGWP that is valid for the full length of your program.
L67: For example, if you complete a 1-year study program in 8 months, you may be able to get a PGWP valid for 1 year.
L68:
